This guide walks you through everything you need to add your research post to this blog — from installing Quarto to opening a pull request.

**Most contributors only need Git and Quarto.** Jupyter and Python are only required if your post includes executable code cells (e.g. plots or computations). Jump to the [optional code setup section](#optional-adding-executable-code) only if you need that.

## 1. Prerequisites

You need the following tools installed once on your machine.

### Git

Check whether Git is installed:

```bash
git --version
```

If not, download it from <https://git-scm.com>.

### Quarto

Download and install Quarto from <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>. It works on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Verify the install:

```bash
quarto --version
```

### A Text Editor

[VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) with the [Quarto extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=quarto.quarto) gives you live preview and syntax highlighting. RStudio also has native Quarto support.

---

## 2. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/UBCMath-Summer-RA-Cohort/research-blog.git
cd research-blog
```

---

## 3. Create Your Branch

Always work on your own branch — never commit directly to `main`.

```bash
git checkout -b firstname-lastname/my-research-topic
```

For example:

```bash
git checkout -b jane-doe/spectral-graph-theory
```

---

## 4. Create Your Post Folder

Posts live in `posts/`. Create a folder with a short, descriptive, lowercase-hyphenated name:

```
posts/
└── spectral-graph-theory/
    └── index.qmd
```

```bash
mkdir posts/spectral-graph-theory
```

---

## 5. Write Your Post

Create `posts/spectral-graph-theory/index.qmd` (or whatever your folder is called) and start with this YAML header:

```yaml
---
title: "Your Post Title"
author: "Your Name"
date: "2026-MM-DD"
description: "One sentence about your project — shown in the post listing."
categories: [your-topic, math]
---
```

> **If your post has executable Python code**, add `jupyter: ubcmath-ra-blog` to the YAML and complete the [optional setup](#optional-adding-executable-code) first.

### YAML Fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | Yes | Shown as the page heading |
| `author` | Yes | Your name |
| `date` | Yes | Format `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `description` | Yes | 1–2 sentences; shown in the listing |
| `categories` | Recommended | Tags for filtering (e.g. `[algebra, combinatorics]`) |
| `image` | Optional | Path to a thumbnail image in your post folder |

### Writing Prose

Quarto uses standard Markdown. A few useful examples:

```markdown
## Section Heading

**Bold text**, *italic text*, and `inline code`.

A paragraph with a [hyperlink](https://quarto.org).
```

### Mathematics

Inline math uses single dollar signs: `$f(x) = x^2$` renders as $f(x) = x^2$.

Display math uses double dollar signs:

```markdown
$$
\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} \, dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}
$$
```

$$
\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} \, dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}
$$

### Adding Images

Put image files in your post folder alongside `index.qmd`, then reference them with standard Markdown:

```markdown
![Caption text](my-figure.png)
```

---

## 6. Preview Locally

From the project root, run:

```bash
quarto preview
```

This opens a live-updating browser preview at `http://localhost:4444` (or similar). Save your file to see changes instantly. Use `Ctrl+C` to stop the server when done.

To render without serving:

```bash
quarto render
```

---

## 7. Commit and Push

Once you are happy with your post:

```bash
# Stage your new files
git add posts/spectral-graph-theory/

# Commit
git commit -m "Add post: Spectral Graph Theory intro"

# Push your branch
git push -u origin firstname-lastname/my-research-topic
```

---

## 8. Open a Pull Request

1. Go to the repository on GitHub.
2. Click **"Compare & pull request"** on your branch.
3. Give the PR a clear title, e.g. `Add post: Spectral Graph Theory`.
4. In the description, summarize your post in a sentence or two.
5. Submit — your supervisor will review and merge.

---

## Optional: Adding Executable Code {#optional-adding-executable-code}

Skip this section unless your post includes live Python computations or plots. It requires conda and Jupyter.

### Step 1: Install the conda environment

The repository ships with an `environment.yml` that installs Python, Jupyter, and scientific packages. If you do not have conda, install [Miniconda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html) first, then run once:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
```

Activate it at the start of every work session:

```bash
conda activate ubcmath-ra-blog
```

### Step 2: Register the Jupyter kernel

Do this once after creating the environment:

```bash
python -m ipykernel install --user --name ubcmath-ra-blog --display-name "ubcmath-ra-blog"
```

Verify it worked:

```bash
quarto check jupyter
```

You should see `ubcmath-ra-blog` listed under known kernels.

### Step 3: Add `jupyter:` to your post's YAML

```yaml
---
title: "Your Post Title"
author: "Your Name"
date: "2026-MM-DD"
description: "One sentence about your project."
categories: [your-topic, math]
jupyter: ubcmath-ra-blog
---
```

### Writing code chunks

Embed executable Python chunks like this:

````markdown
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x), color="steelblue", linewidth=2)
plt.title("Sine Wave")
plt.show()
```
````

Code outputs (plots, tables, printed values) are embedded automatically in the rendered HTML.

**Useful chunk options:**

````markdown
```{python}
#| label: example-chunk
#| echo: false      # hides code, shows output only
#| eval: false      # shows code but does not run it
#| fig-cap: "My figure"
```
````

You can also embed computed values inline so numbers update automatically:

````markdown
```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data/mydata.csv")
mean_val = df["score"].mean()
```
````

```markdown
The dataset contains `{python} len(df)` rows and the mean score is `{python} round(mean_val, 2)`.
```

Put data files in your post folder alongside `index.qmd`:

```
posts/spectral-graph-theory/
    index.qmd
    data/
        mydata.csv
```

---

## Tips and Common Mistakes

- **Broken YAML**: YAML is whitespace-sensitive. Use spaces, not tabs. If `quarto preview` shows a parse error, the frontmatter is usually the culprit.
- **Date format**: Use `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-06-10`), not `June 10` or `10/06/2026`.
- **Math not rendering**: Make sure display math has blank lines above and below the `$$` delimiters.
- **Images not showing**: Confirm the image file is in the same folder as `index.qmd` and the filename matches exactly (case-sensitive on Linux).
- **Kernel not found** *(code posts only)*: Make sure you activated the `ubcmath-ra-blog` environment and ran `python -m ipykernel install` before previewing. See the [optional setup section](#optional-adding-executable-code).

---

## Quick Reference

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Clone repo | `git clone <url>` |
| Create branch | `git checkout -b name/topic` |
| Preview blog | `quarto preview` |
| Render blog | `quarto render` |
| Stage files | `git add posts/your-folder/` |
| Commit | `git commit -m "message"` |
| Push branch | `git push -u origin branch-name` |

**Code posts only:**

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Create environment | `conda env create -f environment.yml` |
| Activate environment | `conda activate ubcmath-ra-blog` |
| Register Jupyter kernel | `python -m ipykernel install --user --name ubcmath-ra-blog --display-name "ubcmath-ra-blog"` |
| Verify kernel | `quarto check jupyter` |
